feasible.reason: The threat is real and the repo evidence checks out line-for-line: fsbl/src/fi.rs:33 returns the constant 0x42 so both wait_random() delays inside check_true_into_sentinel are deterministic (an attacker's second fault needs no new timing); main.rs:220 selects the slot through Option<(Slot,[u8;32])> (Slot is a 2-variant enum, so the Option niche is one byte value away from Some(Slot::A)) and branch.rs:36 into_slot derives the jump address from the enum with no default-fail target; verify.rs:38-108 hashes exactly secure_len/ns_len and never inspects the slot tail; filter_valid (main.rs:321-354) runs one verify_signature path; fsbl/src/main.rs:172 and manifest.rs:30 confirm no MSPLIM; #591 is OPEN. The Trezor precedents cited (boardloader main.c fih_delay/next_stage_addr, bootloader firmware_present/_backup triple ensure, fw_check.c volatile secbool staircase, image.c check_image_contents padding scan, boot_header.c sigmask/sigmask_inv) all exist at the cited lines. Every item is pure firmware on the existing silicon (the RNG peripheral is on-die; needs HSI48 + RCC AHB2ENR1 bit 18 + CCIPR RNGSEL, nothing off-chip), so kind=firmware is correct. Feasibility fits the constraints: the FSBL in this tree links at 20,972 B physical span inside the 32 KiB bench region (the proposal's 28,704 B figure is from another configuration; either way there is >3 KiB headroom), a second verify pass is sequential, not nested, so it reuses the existing ~6 KB verify frame under the 16,376 B budget, and boot cost is +0.375 s per admissible slot (+0.75 s in A/B steady state) plus ~40 ms for a word-wise tail scan. Nothing adds an option-byte or flash write path. Cost M / P1 is right because all of it must land before the WRP→RDP-2 freeze makes the stage unpatchable.
feasible.corrections: (a) Item 5 is mis-framed for C10: WOTS+C has NO checksum chains (sphincs-c10/src/wots.rs:1-5), so 'recompute the WOTS checksum' is not a thing here. The real single-point analogue is the `if sum != TARGET_SUM { return [0u8; N] }` early-return in wots::pk_from_sig (wots.rs:178). A skip of that one branch at the layer-1 WOTS lets an attacker who holds one genuine vendor signature (public, in every manifest page) substitute a chosen layer-0 tree root whose digits are all >= the genuine digits and advance the sigma chains accordingly; the offline grind is ~2^56 hashes (Prod((8-d_i)/8) over 43 digits at average digit 4.77), one-time and reusable against every device since the vendor key is global. Reframe item 5 as 'redundant, TRNG-desynchronised target-sum check + independent digit extraction' rather than checksum redundancy. Note the existing `fault_sweep_c10v.py` 'clean' result does NOT cover this: for the target-sum vector it sweeps only the first 8,000 instructions, and the sum check sits after H_msg/FORS/layer-0 (hundreds of thousands of instructions in), so the #591 sweep must target that instruction window explicitly. (b) sphincs_c10::verify returns bool, not the root; comparing two roots requires a new `verify_root`-style API in sphincs-c10 (which also moves the Aeneas/Lean extraction surface), and ct_eq is unnecessary for public roots (verify.rs already keeps `subtle` out of the FSBL on purpose). (c) Same-code double verify only helps if the two passes are time-desynchronised, so item 1 (TRNG) is a hard prerequisite of item 5, not a sibling. (d) TRNG bring-up in a frozen stage must not copy secure/src/hw/rng.rs (36 KB of source, health-test receipts); it needs the minimal AN4230 CR/HTCR/NSCR sequence inside the CONDRST window (the #698/#704 pq1 seed-error trap, SR=0x41 after idle) with bounded conditioning-reset retries before halting; 'fail = halt' is acceptable only because a dead TRNG also kills secure-world signing, but it should be stated as an accepted brick condition. (e) Jump-to-0 semantics: with TZEN=1, address 0 is the NS alias, so a secure-state `bx` there raises SecureFault, not a reset-vector entry; still fail-closed, but describe it as a fault. (f) Tail scan: the updater erases the whole slot at BEGIN (hw/flash.rs:1366 erase_slot, cmd_fw_begin.rs:11) and pads quadwords with 0xFF, so require 0xFF only, not Trezor's 0x00-or-0xFF. Per-device pages 123-127 are bank-1 pages beyond slot B secure (pages 65-122), so they are outside SLOT_SECURE_CAPACITY, but the scan must start at the manifest's ns_len, and ns_len must cover every linker-placed NS section (the ui-px atlas at slot offset 0x1000..0x14000, and the objcopy `-j` list trap in tools/build-evt-image.sh) or legitimate images will be refused. (g) MSPLIM set in a stage with no fault handlers means overflow -> HardFault -> cortex-m-rt default loop; fail-closed, fine, but say so. (h) Also mention that the parse-only steps verify_structural/verify_crc remain bare `?` returns; harmless, but the staircase should not claim to cover them.
